text:
What do you think about when rent is due?
When the bank takes your pay
And they send bills so fast
That there's no time to pray.
You spend every morning
In a panic of fear
Knowing each day, without hope,
Your home may be gone.
Do I work hard enough?
Can't my savings help?
I've paid taxes and all that
Now where am I supposed
To find any cash for this next bill?
Oh Lordy please guide me
My mind won't let up
Got no idea what to do

When I first started using a computer, at work,
I saw no use for the little icons,
Or how they were so cleverly named.
And that day,
For all time,
The graveyard shift was
a very long night.
Then one morning,
As if from deep in the abyss,
came inspiration.
A series of numbers,
Two digits followed by five,
followed by an equal sign.
They said:
Do not call us,
we will call you.

Brother’s keeper is he who has no father in the faith;
he that would be of like mind, a man hath many names.
Of those which dwell with me have I one brother still
Whom none can call his friend except by my command. He too shall come to pass away,
And when he comes there must we go together.
I will not leave him without help.
He needs it most where first begins our love.
Our common name upon us neither may depart,
Wherefore they say as men and angels are,
So long this day endureth.
When these words speaketh out,
From henceforth God maketh all things new
That for them should arise
Who from themselves were begotten.
There was an angel born,
But yet unmade.

When I look back on my childhood
The fond memories come rushing in
And the one thing that stands out
Above all others is her face
Smiling down at me from afar
Her arms were open to accept
A place by your side was found
In a room with nothing but love
She would wake up before dawn
Prepare breakfast for us
Give advice when needed
With words of strength and hope
There will be many who say
That you can't buy happiness
But as soon as you take it home
Your mom'll make some

When the night is darkest, and it's cold with rain
And the wind howls loud in this autumn time
In a cemetery down by Old Oak Lane
Where she has been laying for many years
A young man named Mike takes up his rake
To sweep away leaves that are falling
Then he sees on the ground as if from heaven
She came to meet him again
Cold case. She hasn't seen her husband since
That day back when they were married
It seems like yesterday but it was 15yrs ago
So sad to think it really happened
Mike says "Hi sweetheart
How did you know I would be here today?"
The first thing she said was
"Are these your clothes?

**Paper Trail**
In the quiet of my desk drawer,
A trail unfolds in every line.
Every scrap of paper bears its mark—
The scent of possibility divine.
First drafts are messy but they speak
Of thoughts unspoken and half-formed dreams
Each sheet a bridge between despair
And visions bright that guide our streams.
Proofs come later with more finesse
But still mistakes within them hide
Those edits turn each page to gold
Yet sometimes doubt can make us sigh.
Footnotes add context where we may have fallen short
Endings suggest new ways ahead
Together these pages form one story

The time of the game had run out. This is an eternity compared to our everyday life, but in a football match it's just too brief.
This is where overtime comes into play.
After that we have extra minutes with stoppage at half-time and after every goal until one team leads by more than 3 goals.
And then there's also penalty shootouts.
Every second counts in this madness.
Let us remember all those guys who were forced for their careers to think fast when they are given these few seconds.
They can either get a goal or end up on the bench.
Football players live in such conditions.
You may call them "lucky", if you want.
But don't forget that these men put everything on the line.
Please rate

Comments:
The song "Last Bus Home" tells the story of a person who has been abandoned and left without support. The lyrics describe how this individual was not provided with food, care or companionship when they needed it most. Instead, they were cast aside as if their life had no value.
As time passed by, the lonely soul found themselves on different buses, trying various routes, but still unable to find security for themselves. It seemed impossible at first glance.
But then one day something happened; just before getting off work there arrived another vehicle called 'The Golden Rule'. Its driver offered them a warm meal and asked about what trouble kept bringing them here.

My love for my son is so deep, the bond that I share with him.
I will stand by his side in every fight he'll ever face.
And as a mother, it's hard to watch when your child suffers.
But through this ordeal we can be strong.
So do not give up on yourself.
Your future holds many wonders.
For this momentary pain
Is what leads us there.

When I walk the halls
Of a hospital,
I am walking in
Somebody else's world.
Each patient is
An old acquaintance,
Who has left us
Without any explanation.
The sterile air,
As you inhale it,
Seems to carry
A subtle sadness.
And yet each day,
Each time I pass,
Another person
Takes my place. Another

When you play in the pawn shop
Take off your clothes and get into bed
The money gets there when you are dreaming
And it’s all yours if you can keep it
But don’t give up hope just yet
Because we’ll pay what we promise
All those people who want to see
Are lining up at the door
Don't be too sad
There's always a second chance
You only have one life
Make sure you use it well
In this song, why do they suggest taking their clothes down? What does that mean?
So, let me explain. The singer is talking about playing cards in a game called "pawns," where instead of using regular chips or coins for bets, players use things like jewelry or expensive items as collateral.
Taking off your clothes means going back to wearing simple clothing again - basically being honest with yourself and others involved in the deal.
It also implies letting go of any pretenses or lies; showing vulnerability by revealing true self.

I sit on the floor, in my bedroom,
witnessing your final breaths.
The glass shattering as you fall,
my broken heart can't help but weep.
Now I see that I was a fool
to think this would last forever,
for every human needs
a space of their own.
Do not look at me,
do not listen to what I say,
but know
that there is hope for all,
though it may be hard
and take time.
Hope means
you never lose yourself.

Caring can also sometimes mean giving up control.
Give me back my power - I am strong.

until we figure things out,
and make us both feel better.
Or maybe she has left because she feels

I am in my third semester of medical school, and I've been thinking a lot about the future lately. This has led me to ask myself an important question that is crucial for success as either a student or physician:
"Will you walk into your shift ready?"
As students and physicians we are all too familiar with this feeling when it comes to starting work after taking time off from our studies.
Everyday things pile up on us whether they be emails on computer accounts, pending test results, upcoming tests, patient charts to review…etc.
All these tasks seem overwhelming at first so we procrastinate by doing something else until later – usually dinner before bed.
But what if instead every day was filled completely?
What would be different?
My goal is always clear when beginning shifts - stay hydrated.
So why do others take longer?
The most common reason:
They wake-up late.
In those last few moments left over from their busy night they get dressed & brush teeth while sifting through email notifications.
By not giving themselves enough prep-time during sleep many end up making one simple mistake...
